messages:
Anita: heads-up — p99 spike observed for ap-southeast -> us-east fallbacks. p99 ~1400ms; baseline ~600ms. Profiling shows a big chunk from kernel handoff + KV cache misses (≈700–900ms).
Tomás: can you paste the perf trace? short snippet is fine.
Anita: attaching quick trace sample:
```
[trace] req=8f3c kernel_swap_start=1611623423 kernel_swap_end=1611623428 kv_miss=true kv_load_ms=240 tail_wait_ms=420 total_ms=1130
[trace] req=9b2a kernel_swap_start=1611623450 kernel_swap_end=1611623454 kv_miss=false kv_load_ms=20 tail_wait_ms=60 total_ms=240
```
Kevin: interesting — the bad ones show kernel_swap + kv_miss. Also seeing microbatch targets at 16 during those windows. microbatch size seems correlated with longer kernel swap queuing.
Marcos: +1 on kv_miss amplification. Remote fallbacks bypass local kvcache, so we get more misses and heavier disk reads for weights/compilation artifacts.
perf-bot: perf-alert: p99_latency(ap-southeast->us-east) = 1400ms (threshold 1200ms) :rotating_light:
Anita: proposed quick experiments:
- reduce microbatch_target from 16 -> 8 for this route
- prefer_same_kernel_on_fallback = true (avoid kernel swap when possible)
- add short compile-warmup for target kernels
Command I used to push a test change:
```
curl -s -X POST https://admin.redwood/api/v1/route-config -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -d '{"route":"ap-southeast->us-east","microbatch_target":8,"prefer_same_kernel":true}'
```
Tomás: preferring same-arch kernel makes sense but only if compiled kernel cache exists in the target region. What kernel variants do we have prebuilt in us-east?
Kevin: current compiled kernels: ["quant-avx2-v2","copper-ampere-fp16","reorder-int8-v1"] — for ampere hardware prefer copper-ampere-fp16 to avoid swap.
Marcos: I'll add a precompile job to seed copper-ampere-fp16 in us-east for the affected model families. Also will check kvcache retention TTLs; cross-region fetch seems to evict more aggressively.
Anita: quick A/B results (30m window): lowered mb + prefer_same_kernel -> p99 dropped from 1400ms to ~980ms. p95 is basically unchanged. Not perfect but big win on tail.
Kevin: that suggests p99 dominated by kernel swap + kvcache. The unchanged p95 implies steady-state latency unaffected.
Tomás: next steps: dig into the small subset of requests still in the tail. Add deeper traces for those req ids and check disk I/O patterns (NFS vs local SSD).
Marcos: also suggest we adjust routing threshold: current fallback trigger is local_util > 0.85. If we raise to 0.9 we reduce unnecessary cross-region fallbacks; or better: require capacity headroom + compiled-kernel-availability.
Kevin: tweak batching hysteresis as well — microbatch max wait currently 12ms; try max_wait_ms=8 to reduce head-of-line queueing for short requests.
Anita: scheduling a canary rollout of these three changes (mb_target=8, prefer_same_kernel, max_wait_ms=8) for the ap-southeast route. Will monitor p99/p999 and KV miss rate. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
perf-bot: rollout-started: route=ap-southeast->us-east canary_id=canary-20260318-01
Tomás: once canary stabilizes we should codify a fallback policy: prefer same-kernel + compiled-cache presence before routing cross-region. Otherwise prefer local slower model variant instead of swapping kernels.
Marcos: noted — I'll open an infra task to add compiled-cache-awareness into the router and add a warmup precompile job for high-usage models.
Anita: good plan. I’ll post follow-up with 3-hour and 24-hour rollup metrics.
